messages:
alyssa: Quick heads-up — seeing free-tier requests in eu-west get routed to the tiny-quantized variant and then immediately hit a fallback to cpu-fallback. Not sure if quota enforcement or routing policy is at fault.
max: Do we have the policy JSON that free tenants use? Could be a priority ordering issue.
ravi: It’s the default per-tenant policy right now: free -> pro-quant-small -> enterprise-quant -> cpu-fallback. But quota enforcement triggers on token spikes and triggers fallback.
sophia: pasting current policy for one example tenant:
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "free-123",
  "routing": [
    {"variant": "redwood/quant-small", "weight": 0.7, "min_slo_ms": 150},
    {"variant": "redwood/quant-tiny", "weight": 0.2, "min_slo_ms": 120},
    {"variant": "redwood/cpu-fallback", "weight": 0.1, "min_slo_ms": 500}
  ],
  "quota": {"monthly_tokens": 1000000, "burst_per_min": 5000}
}
```
alyssa: Right — we don’t explicitly set an "allow_fallback": false flag so the router will use cpu-fallback once the selected GPU pool is saturated. That’s intended, but UX is confusing for customers who expected degraded model, not CPU.
maria-ui: UX idea: add a console toggle per-tier "prefer degraded model over cpu fallback" + a preview of the expected routing path and estimated latency/cost. Preview could call the same routing decision API with a synthetic request.
max: Preview API is fine but we need to standardize telemetry first. Current logs don't include "fallback_reason" consistently.
ravi: Suggestion: emit route.decision with fields [tenant_id, tier, region, chosen_variant, fallback_chain, reason_code, tokens_requested, tokens_billed]. And emit quota.exceeded events with threshold type (burst/min, monthly).
sophia: Agree. We should add reason_code values: "capacity", "quota", "model_unavailable", "policy_block".
max: Also need a graceful enforcement mode for free tier: instead of immediate hard fail/fallback, apply a 30s grace window per-tenant where we allow last-known good variant to complete. That handles spikes and avoids flipping users between models.
alyssa: How would that look config-wise?
ravi: Something like:
```json
"quota_enforcement": {
  "mode": "soft", // soft | hard
  "grace_seconds": 30,
  "burst_window": 60
}
```
maria-ui: In the console, map that to a slider: "grace period" (0-120s) + enforcement mode radio. Show tooltip: "soft = retries + short grace; hard = immediate fallback or rejection".
max: Ops concern: soft mode increases routing state and KV for grace timers per-tenant. We need to measure memory impact. Can ops-bot run estimate?
ops-bot: @max running estimate script... result: expected KV entries ~ active_tenants * (grace_seconds / average_request_interval). For free tier worst-case ~ 60k entries, memory ~ 120MB.
max: That's acceptable but we should gate soft mode by plan type (only free/pro, not enterprise).
sophia: Rollout plan: ship telemetry + routing decision API changes, then feature-flag soft-enforcement, enable for 10% of free traffic (canary). After 24h, evaluate dashboard: fallback.rate, avg_latency_by_variant, token_overage_events.
alyssa: Add label on telemetry for canary_percent and policy_version.
ravi: Also add a console warning when a tenant pins a variant (enterprise pin) — pinning should bypass fallback chain unless "allow_pin_bypass" is false. Need explicit consent for bypassing fallback (security/compliance customers care).
maria-ui: UX: show a red badge "pinned" and a checkbox "allow auto-fallback if pinned variant becomes unavailable".
max: Internal API debate: Should routing decision API be idempotent and deterministic (pure function of policy + load snapshot) or allowed to mutate internal grace timers? If pure, we need separate side-channel to start grace windows.
ravi: I'd vote for pure function + side-channel. Keeps decision testing easier. Side-channel = /routing/evict/start-grace with tenant_id, request_id.
sophia: Tests: add unit tests for policy precedence (tier overrides region), and e2e with simulated spike that asserts soft grace prevents immediate cpu fallback for N requests.
alyssa: Action items: @sophia implement telemetry schema PR, @ravi add soft-enforcement config and side-channel API, @maria-ui add console wireframe + preview API link, @max schedule canary for 10% free on staging next Tue.
maria-ui: I'll prototype the preview modal today and share frames. :thumbsup:
max: thanks. follow up in #eng-qa for canary metrics.
alyssa: closing loop — we'll reconvene after canary metrics. If fallback.rate drops but latency rises too much we tweak grace_seconds.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: canary rollout scheduled at 2026-03-24T03:00:00Z for feature-flag "soft-quota-enforcement-free-v2".
max: cool, I'll add dashboard panels: telemetry.route.decision.fallback_rate (by region, tier), telemetry.quota.exceeded.count, cost.delta-per-variant.
ravi: one more: add cluster hint to telemetry (gpu_pool_id) so we can trace if capacity issues are localized.
sophia: noted. I'll include gpu_pool_id and policy_version in the schema PR.
alyssa: Great work team, thanks!
